summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for diuresis in preparation for a right heart catheterization required to maintain eligibility for liver transplantation. He has a history of HCV-related cirrhosis with complications including ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, grade II esophageal varices, and portopulmonary hypertension on Remodulin therapy. During admission, he underwent a therapeutic paracentesis with removal of 2 liters of fluid and had a tunneled central line placed for long-term Remodulin delivery. Right heart catheterization showed stable pulmonary pressures with a mean PA pressure of 30 mmHg, supporting continued transplant candidacy. Hypokalemia developed during diuresis and was managed with potassium supplementation and temporary discontinuation of torsemide. Blood cultures remained negative, and a previously noted renal mass was confirmed as a benign simple cyst. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor potassium levels, hold torsemide until electrolytes stabilize, and resume outpatient follow-up with the liver transplant team.
